text:
maria: Heads up — I found S3 backup snapshots encrypted with a KMS ciphertext referencing an old CMK ARN. Looks like some legacy import jobs still used the pre-rotation key. Object: backups/2026-03-20/import-job-rls-2026-03-20.tar.gz, KMS ARN: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-legacy-cmk
aj: Can you paste the exact object key + CMK ARN? Is this from the on-prem import pipeline?
maria: Here: `backups/2026-03-20/import-job-rls-2026-03-20.tar.gz`\n`arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-legacy-cmk`\nFound in export job logs from `import-runner-v1` around 03:12 UTC. Suspect window ~03:00-03:30.
sam: Do we have Vault transit wrapping for backups or was it KMS-only? If KMS-only we need a re-encrypt path.
maria: It's KMS-only (legacy pipeline). The new pipeline uses Vault transit but these older snapshots predate rollout.
kevin: Ok. Proposed plan:
1) inventory affected snapshots (list + tags)
2) create rewrap job with dedicated service account `infra-rewrap-sa`
3) re-encrypt blobs using new CMK `arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/new-archive-cmk`
4) update metadata pointers and terraform references
5) revoke old CMK access when done
Need to ensure restores still work during/after rewrap.
aj: Also need an RBAC sweep — who currently has Decrypt on the old CMK? Initial hits: `infra-archive-sa`, `partner-ingest-sa`, `legacy-ingest-user`. I'll run IAM queries now.
sec-bot: Created ticket SEC-2026: backup-cmk-rewrap — https://tracker.redwood.example/SEC-2026
maria: Timeline: aim for canary rewrap tonight. Blocker: ensure restore smoke tests in staging before mass rewrap. Can't risk corrupting restores.
sam: I can run the rewrap in staging. Need kms:Decrypt on old CMK and kms:Encrypt on new CMK for the job role. No Vault policy changes required since we're not using Vault for these objects.
aj: I'll revoke long-lived creds used by the import job and rotate the service-account keys. Also tagging: `cmk-legacy-exposed` on affected snapshots.
kevin: Also enable KMS key usage logging + S3 access logs for the affected bucket and increase retention to 90 days for the incident window.
maria: Noted. Found a public gist that referenced `legacy-archive-sa` — it's been removed, and the key was rotated earlier but snapshot copies remained. Adding that to SEC-2026.
sam: Pseudocode for rewrap (staging):
```
# re-encrypt using aws kms re-encrypt
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://old_blob.bin --source-key-id arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd-legacy-cmk \
  --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:...:key/new-archive-cmk --output text > new_blob.bin
# upload new_blob.bin back to S3 and update snapshot metadata
```
aj: After rewrap we'll: update datastore metadata, update infra TF to point to new snapshot IDs, and schedule a key policy lockdown to remove cross-account principals.
maria: Can we also add an entry in the incident log noting rewrap operator, job id, and SHA checksum of re-encrypted blobs? We should keep an audit trail even though Vault wasn't involved.
kevin: Agreed. SLA: complete canary + smoke restores by 04:00 UTC. If we hit issues, pause and escalate to oncall.
maria: No objections. Starting canary rewrap now. I'll post results here. :thumbsup:
sec-bot: Reminder — run a secret-scan across repos for any references to the old CMK ARN / `legacy-archive-sa` (dotfiles, gists, slack snippets).
aj: On it. Will post IAM change logs + rotated key ARNs back to SEC-2026.
maria: Update: canary rewrap completed on 3 snapshots, smoke restore passed for 2 of 3 (one had a packaging mismatch, investigating). Will not mass rewrap until resolved.
kevin: Thanks. Keep updates in the ticket. Once packaging mismatch fixed, proceed with bulk rewrap and then revoke old CMK access.
